name: Clinical X-ray computed tomography
summary: EMI's scanner combined X-ray readings from many angles by computer into brain cross-sections, letting doctors see soft tissue inside the skull from 1971-72.
description: Computer-reconstructed X-ray transmission measurements from multiple angles, configured for clinically useful brain soft-tissue cross-sectional imaging.

links.statement: Hounsfield adapted X-ray attenuation measurement and computation to reconstruct cross-sections that address the overlap of structures in projection radiographs.
links.scope: Method-level relationship between medical projection X-ray imaging and computed X-ray slices; not the particular 1896 patient apparatus.
links.alternatives: Other medical imaging methods and reconstruction designs existed or emerged.
links.caveats: Other tomography and mathematical reconstruction methods existed earlier; no sole-cause or global invention claim.
links.timing: The 1896 clinical application and CT’s early-1970s use are separate stages.

evidence.supports: Hounsfield explicitly contrasts projection overlap with multi-angle computed reconstruction and describes the X-ray source.
